checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: The central question is 'Can they steal the guild's ledger without becoming its new masters?'. ch 15: Devan takes the book and hands it to Neela in front of the forty. ch 18 and ch 25-26: she does become a master in all but name ('Your tea, Master'; 'I've become him, Devan'), which keeps the question live. ch 27: the bargain holds. Neela takes Vellan's page from Devan's hand ('She felt his grip. It was iron, for a moment... Then it opened.') and no one is caged. ch 28: she reads every page aloud by daylight and gives each one to its owner, Vellan and Kirri included. Chathu goes to the Justice and Pachan keeps the groves with no master. She keeps only the contract books and the sealed green quire. ch 32: she adds a recall vote ('Any time the forty say so, by your vote, I put down the ledger and the plank and walk away'). The open threads (the queen's thirty pages, the hunt by the crown) belong to the series hinge, not to this book's question.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: C01 langurs: ch 2 answers who walked the closed road (Rema and her escort by the goat path), and ch 32 repeats the silence as Vellan walks up. C02 Ammu's pouch: ch 7 'It was light, and loose in her fingers... I'm keeping it anyway.' C03 First Guard's wrist seam: ch 32 'a palace surgeon pares the old ridges smooth, so a slipped cuff shows one seam.' C04 hounds and C08 nightbark on the escort: ch 32 reveals the escort are the queen's odiyan night-guard. C05 nightbark salve and C18 Eravi's leave to ride the wood road: ch 22 satchel 'reeks', ch 24 Eravi confesses buying from the House 'and paying in news'. C06 'Ask your captain': ch 9 the grey packet ('Say nothing, and your wife is kept'). C07 second sealed case: ch 30 the queen's writ is opened. C09 book in the well house: ch 14-15. C10 Pachan's sweet: ch 28 'Pachan lifted the bar himself, and the gate dragged open.' C11 Muthu and the cart order: ch 24 Eravi 'passed on the cart order'. C12 Janu's ten paces: ch 23. C13 new grate: ch 23-24 'Only the physician keeps that key.' C14 sharp-milled silver: ch 11 matches it to the scouts' die; the payoff lands in ch 21 ('coin that was new and silver and never handled'), not ch 20 as outlined. C15 the eleven contracts: ch 16 and ch 18. C16 green quire: ch 32 'Sold to the crown.' C17 Vellan's entries: ch 27 'Thirty. Release not to be granted. Sell to the crown when spent.' C19 sunbird marks in the tally book: ch 20 'By leave... Nellimala, second harvest.' C20, C21 and C22 are logged as series threads. No clue is left with neither a payoff nor a thread.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: ch 16 (the outline midpoint): Neela reads Asha's contract aloud with her hand sliding down the leaf: 'Hand, Thirty... Lookout,' she read. 'Seventeen.' This recasts the parrot newel, the hollow eleventh step and her wide path round the west stair. It changes the romance. Devan 'set the leaves down... "I need to walk"' and goes into the rain without his cloak. ch 17: 'I won't answer that' to whether he can look at her. He puts the pebble in his cheek although she took no resin, sleeps across her threshold, and their ease is gone until ch 23-24.

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: The opening belief is stated outright in ch 18: 'Chathu chose... Vellan struck... I won't carry what was put in my hands in the dark. It isn't mine.' The choice that proves the change comes in ch 29. She stands unasked, against Devan's offer to carry it for her, and reads the lookout line into the crown record herself: "Seventeen is a number. It was mine for twenty-one years." ... "My name is Neela. I'm the lookout. I was told to open a lamp twice if anyone came into the court. I wasn't told what the lamp was for. I didn't ask. I do not offer that as a reason." The ch 23 confession to Janu prepares it: 'I was good at my work, and I did it well, and I never once asked whose stair it was.' The ch 28 daylight reading is the repair she makes for the forty. Note: the strongest proof lands in ch 29 (with ch 23 as preparation), not ch 28 as the outline's proof_chapter says.

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: ch 28: Kirri stays a civet. 'A caging could not be undone, and a page in the straw could not undo it... The civet blinked once. Then it curled round and slept.' Other losses also stay lost. Ittan is executed (ch 5). Thilak burns his page and his village with it (ch 28). In ch 30 Devan is stripped of Kettamala and the warden's seal and gives the iron disc to Muthu. None of these is reversed.

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: Devan's goal is to prove who bought Asha's murder before the court. It runs from ch 1 ('Asha's contract... I need that entry... A court will take paper') to the payoff in ch 29: Rema records 'Asha, daughter of the late warden of Kettamala... Killed under contract. Her name is written.' The goal predates the heroine and does not depend on her. His other goals are to hold the pass for the border villages (ch 19, ch 30 'Hold the pass... For the villages below it') and to take the sunbird writ to the high court.

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: ch 32: Neela and Devan break the green seal and find 'Sold to the crown' with thirty numbers that match thirty stubs cut from the ledger. Vellan confirms the queen's night-guard are odiyans, the escort among them, and 'Their pages... In her leaf... she witnessed every one of their first turnings.' The queen can trace the scent-post trail by the new moon. Neela vows: 'I will read every one of the thirty their page, by daylight, to their face.' This opens a bigger question for book 2 while this book's own question stays answered.

series_threads.thread: The First Guard's 'It passes' to Neela (ch 5). Ch 32 shows she is one of the queen's thirty sold odiyans who has survived the ache, but her name, her shape and her personal stake are left for book 2's attempt to free the night-guard.

Devan keeps back the sunbird payment writ (with Chathu's chit and the cut seal) for the high court in full session (ch 29). He packs it when he leaves (ch 31). No court will now hear it, so its use against the queen carries into the next book.

The forty ride out with one season's flasks while the groves stay with Pachan (ch 28, ch 32 inventory). Neela gives up her own flask and the ache is coming for all of them. Who supplies resin after the season is an open series problem.

summary: The book meets every structural promise. It answers its central question in ch 27-28. Neela becomes the guild's master in all but name, admits it, and then empties the ledger by daylight readings, keeping no page. The only questions left open are the queen's thirty pages and the crown hunt, which form the series hinge in ch 32. Every planted clue C01-C19 pays off on the page and C20-C22 are logged as series threads. Two items differ from the outline: C14's payoff is explicit in ch 21 rather than ch 20, and the heroine's clearest transformation proof is her unasked reading of 'Lookout, Seventeen' into the crown record in ch 29 (prepared by the ch 23 confession to Janu), not ch 28. The ch 16 midpoint reverses the romance. Kirri's lasting caging, Ittan's death and Devan's lost office are real losses that stay lost. Devan's goal of getting Asha's murder on record is independent of the heroine and is fulfilled in ch 29. One small continuity note for the owner: in ch 1 Neela plans to spend a smear that night, ch 2 says she kept both, and ch 6 says she spent one on the night of the execution. The sequence is reconcilable but worth a line edit.
